title: Your First Weekend at St Lawrence University, Shared as Cards
description: A low-key, under-21-safe first-weekend sequence built around campus landmarks, first-year activities, food, reflection, and shared time.

cards.title: Start at the Sullivan Student Center
cards.subtitle: Friday arrival • student hub
cards.notes: Use the Information Desk as a practical first stop, then find the lounge and meeting areas so you know where student programming and services are based.
cards.short_summary: Orient yourself in the campus’s central student space.
cards.evidence_claim: The Sullivan Student Center provides student study, lounge, meeting, event, dining, mail, and Student Life spaces.
cards.source_title: Sullivan Student Center | St. Lawrence University
cards.access_notes: Student spaces and room use are subject to University access and reservation policies.

cards.title: Have your first campus dinner at Dana
cards.subtitle: Friday evening • campus dining
cards.notes: Meet a classmate for a meal and look over the dining setup together; Dana serves buffet-style meals and lists daily menus through Dining Services.
cards.short_summary: A straightforward first shared meal on campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Dana is St. Lawrence’s main dining hall, open seven days a week, with buffet-style meals and daily menu information.
cards.access_notes: Meals are obtained through a meal plan or guest payment; check current Dining Services information.

cards.title: Pause at Gunnison Memorial Chapel
cards.subtitle: Friday evening • campus landmark
cards.notes: Walk through the chapel grounds and save a moment for quiet reflection. Check the campus calendar before entering for an event or gathering.
cards.short_summary: A historic place for a calm first-night reset.
cards.evidence_claim: Gunnison Memorial Chapel opened in 1926 and serves campus and community gatherings; student bell ringers play its bells on weekdays during classes.
cards.source_title: Gunnison Memorial Chapel History and Photos | St. Lawrence University
cards.access_notes: Gathering and event access varies; consult the Chaplain’s Office or campus calendar.

cards.title: See Herring-Cole Hall in daylight
cards.subtitle: Saturday morning • historic campus
cards.notes: Take a daylight walk to this historic building and, when available, settle into the Cole Reading Room for quiet reading or individual desk work.
cards.short_summary: Pair a campus walk with a historic reading room.
cards.evidence_claim: Herring-Cole Hall is listed on the National Register of Historic Places, and the Cole Reading Room is designated for quiet study during the academic year.
cards.access_notes: The Cole Reading Room is for individual desk work and reading; observe posted building access rules.

cards.title: Make Owen D. Young Library your study anchor
cards.subtitle: Saturday late morning • library stop
cards.notes: Find a study floor, then note the ground-floor meditation and prayer space for a quiet break between orientation tasks and new conversations.
cards.short_summary: Locate a reliable academic and quiet-space resource.
cards.evidence_claim: Owen D. Young Library has a ground-floor space with meditation cushions and prayer mats that students may use for breathing, meditation, and Muslim prayer.
cards.access_notes: Library access and services may vary by academic calendar and campus ID status.

cards.title: Look for the current Brush Art Gallery exhibition
cards.subtitle: Saturday afternoon • campus art
cards.notes: Check the gallery’s current exhibition information before you go, then use the visit as an easy conversation starter with a new friend or roommate.
cards.short_summary: See rotating art on campus and take in a visual change of pace.
cards.evidence_claim: The Richard F. Brush Art Gallery is on campus and has a permanent collection of more than 7,000 objects alongside regularly rotating exhibitions.
cards.source_title: Art and Art History | St. Lawrence University
cards.access_notes: Confirm current exhibition dates and gallery access before visiting.

cards.title: Take a breather in the North Country Garden
cards.subtitle: Saturday afternoon • Sykes Hall courtyard
cards.notes: Bring a water bottle or a book and use the garden for a short reset. It is intended as a quiet outdoor place to sit, eat, meditate, or study.
cards.short_summary: A designated campus spot for a gentle outdoor pause.
cards.evidence_claim: St. Lawrence identifies the North Country Garden near Sykes Hall as an outdoor space students may use to sit, meditate, eat lunch, or study.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor use depends on weather and normal campus access conditions.

cards.title: Join a First-Year Cup activity
cards.subtitle: Saturday • first-year tradition
cards.notes: Ask your First-Year Program or resident staff what Cup activity is next, then join the option that feels comfortable—games, trivia, banner making, or songs.
cards.short_summary: A school-specific way to meet peers during the opening days.
cards.evidence_claim: First-Year Cup begins in students’ first days on campus and includes lawn games, trivia, banner-designing, and song competition.
cards.access_notes: Participation details and timing are set by the First-Year Program each semester.

cards.title: Pick a Backyard Adventure
cards.subtitle: Saturday • first-week group outing
cards.notes: Choose a listed group outing that suits your energy and access needs. The program includes options such as hiking, screen-printing, pottery, escape rooms, and apple picking.
cards.short_summary: A structured way to explore the North Country with new people.
cards.evidence_claim: St. Lawrence’s First-Year Program describes Backyard Adventures as first-week group outings including screen-printing, escape rooms, hiking, pottery, virtual reality, ropes courses, and apple picking.
cards.access_notes: Offerings, registration, transportation, and any fees vary by outing; confirm with the First-Year Program.

cards.title: Close with a Shared Sunday activity
cards.subtitle: Sunday afternoon • connect beyond class
cards.notes: Check the week’s Shared Sunday plans and bring a friend. Choose a relaxed activity such as board games, crocheting, canoeing, or hiking if offered.
cards.short_summary: End the weekend with a low-pressure shared activity.
cards.evidence_claim: Shared Sunday invites students, faculty, and staff to Sunday-afternoon activities including canoeing, hiking, board games, and crocheting.
cards.access_notes: Activities and availability vary; consult First-Year Program communications for the current schedule.
